A child leans over a drawing, puzzle, or carefully stacked blocks. Their eyebrows draw slightly together, and their eyes track one small point rather than the camera. As one hand makes a precise movement, the tip of the tongue slips between relaxed lips, often toward one corner of the mouth. The other hand steadies the paper or object; shoulders lift a little, then settle. Breathing is quiet, with an occasional soft hum or whispered word. The tongue retreats when the child pauses or looks up. Small finger corrections and natural, uneven timing make the concentration believable.

After finishing something well, a person inhales and straightens, lifting the breastbone and drawing the shoulders gently back. The chest looks fuller without becoming rigid; the chin rises slightly. Their eyes brighten and glance toward the result, then toward someone nearby. A restrained smile spreads across the mouth, sometimes followed by a small pleased laugh or a warm, steady “I did it.” Hands may rest at the hips, hang loosely, or briefly smooth a shirt. The pose holds for a beat before the breath leaves the chest and the shoulders soften again. Clothing stretches subtly across the upper torso.

A person pauses after an unsuccessful attempt. Their shoulders drop and roll forward as they exhale; the upper back curves, making the head appear lower. Their eyes leave the failed task and settle on the floor or their empty hands. The mouth closes into a thin line or parts for a quiet sigh. Fingers loosen around what they were holding, and the arms hang with little tension. For a few seconds they stay still, then shift their weight or take a slow step. If they speak, the voice is low and brief, with less energy than a moment earlier.

At the instant good news lands, a person’s eyes widen and their face opens into a grin. They curl one hand into a fist and drive it upward from near the waist to chest or shoulder height, bending the elbow sharply. The shoulder rises with the motion, while the other arm balances the body. A quick “Yes!” or delighted shout arrives with the upward thrust. The fist may give one short second bounce, then relax; fingers uncurl as the person laughs or looks toward companions. Hair and loose sleeves follow the abrupt movement a fraction of a second later.

A person bends their knees quickly, pushes against the ground, and springs upward when something wonderful happens. Their eyes brighten, cheeks lift, and the mouth opens in a broad smile or shout. Hands rise freely, either overhead or out to the sides; fingers spread rather than holding a fixed pose. Clothing and hair lag behind the ascent, then lift briefly as the body falls. They land with a light thud and bent knees that absorb the impact, sometimes making a second, smaller hop. Excited laughter, a short cheer, and quick breathing accompany the movement. Nearby people may turn or smile.

A happy dance is a brief, improvised burst rather than a polished routine. The person shifts weight from foot to foot, takes two or three small sideways steps, and lets the knees bounce in uneven rhythm. Shoulders sway; hands lift, flick outward, or tap lightly near the chest. Their eyes crinkle toward someone nearby, and the mouth stays open in a grin between laughs or playful, wordless sounds. Shoes may scuff or tap the floor, while loose clothing sways after each turn. The steps change when balance changes, then slow naturally as the person catches their breath.

Excitement brings both hands up in front of the chest or face, palms facing each other. The person claps in a quick, slightly irregular series of sharp, light slaps, with fingers sometimes missing full contact. Their elbows bounce, shoulders lift, and the body may rock forward or make tiny hops. Eyes stay wide and fixed on the happy event; raised cheeks and an open smile show delight. A high, breathy laugh, squeal, or rapid “Again!” falls between claps. The rhythm speeds up briefly, then breaks as they turn to share the moment with someone beside them.

Two people face each other after a shared success. One raises an open hand beside the shoulder, palm forward and fingers spread; the other mirrors it while looking at the offered palm. Both extend their arms, adjusting their aim until the palms meet with a crisp, flat slap. Elbows flex slightly on contact, absorbing the force, and the hands separate at once. Their eyes meet afterward, mouths lifting into smiles or opening for a laugh, cheer, or brief “Nice!” Bodies lean in during the reach and ease back afterward. Sleeves and loose hair move subtly with the quick arm motion.

Two people turn toward each other, make brief eye contact and extend closed fists at chest height. Their knuckles meet lightly for a moment, then their arms pull back; the contact is a soft tap, not a punch. Fingers stay curled, wrists mostly straight, and shoulders relaxed. One may lift their eyebrows or smile, with a quiet laugh or a short spoken greeting in a warm voice. Bodies lean in just enough to bridge the gap without stepping into each other. In daylight, the small shadows between their knuckles disappear at contact and return as their hands separate.

Three or more people step close until their shoulders and upper arms touch. Arms curve around backs or rest across shoulders; hands lie open against fabric rather than gripping tightly. Faces turn sideways to make room, eyes may close briefly, and mouths soften into smiles. The cluster sways a few centimetres as people adjust their footing, with clothes rustling, small laughs and overlapping words in gentle voices. Someone at the edge may reach across another person’s back to join. In natural indoor or outdoor light, faces are partly shaded by neighbouring heads, while the outer shoulders remain more brightly lit.

Standing or walking side by side, one friend lifts an arm over the other’s near shoulder. The forearm rests loosely across the upper back, with an open hand near the far shoulder; it does not pull the neck down. Their shoulders draw closer and their steps briefly fall into the same rhythm. Both may glance at each other, then look ahead, with relaxed eyes and slight smiles. A low comment or short laugh accompanies the movement, alongside footsteps and fabric brushing fabric. In daylight, the raised arm casts a narrow shadow across the friend’s shirt.

Two people walk side by side with their nearest elbows bent and loosely linked. Their forearms angle forward, hands relaxed and fingers uncurling slightly as they move. The link limits how far their arms swing, so they match pace with small adjustments in stride. Heads turn toward each other during conversation; eyes meet briefly, mouths move in quiet speech, and smiles come and go. Shoes make alternating taps on pavement, with an occasional soft brush of sleeves. In afternoon light, their joined arms form one compact shape between their bodies, while their leg shadows stretch separately across the ground.

A family pair walks close together, often an adult beside a child. The adult lowers one arm; the child reaches up, and their fingers wrap comfortably around each other’s hands without squeezing. Their joined hands swing gently with their steps, rising a little when they step over a kerb. The adult glances down to check the child’s position; the child looks ahead or up, with an open expression and a small smile. Soft conversation, footsteps and the rustle of clothing accompany them. In street or park light, their hands stay visible between them, at about the child’s shoulder height.

A rider climbs onto another person’s back while the carrier bends forward slightly. The rider’s arms rest over the carrier’s shoulders, hands clasped loosely in front, and legs hang along the carrier’s sides. The carrier supports the rider beneath the thighs and takes shorter, springier steps to keep balance. Both faces show alert, playful smiles; the rider looks ahead over one shoulder, while the carrier watches the path. Breathing becomes a little louder, mixed with footsteps, clothing rustle and brief laughter or playful words. As they move through daylight, the rider’s legs bounce gently with each step, never swinging independently of the carrier’s pace.

A younger relative walks beside a grandmother, carrying her shopping bags by their handles. The bag handles pull downward on the carrier’s fingers, and the bags sway a little behind each step; heavier ones hang closer to the leg. The carrier keeps shoulders level and glances toward her with a small smile, speaking in an ordinary, attentive voice. She walks at her own pace, looking ahead or toward the relative, her mouth moving in reply. Her hands may be free or hold a handbag. Footsteps, light plastic or fabric rustling, and quiet conversation are audible. Daylight shows the bags’ folds and shifting contents.

A younger person approaches an elder and gently takes the elder’s offered hand with one or both hands. They lower their head, briefly touch their lips to the back of the hand, then lift their face and release it without tugging. Their eyes glance down during the kiss and return to the elder’s face; the mouth settles into a modest smile. The elder’s fingers remain relaxed, and the elder may smile or speak a quiet greeting or blessing. Clothing shifts softly as both lean toward each other. In indoor or daylight settings, the gesture lasts only a moment, with their hands clearly visible between them.

An adult bends slightly toward a child at a comfortable height, with relaxed shoulders and a soft, closed-mouth smile. Their eyes settle on the child’s forehead, then close briefly as their lips touch the skin for about a second. One hand may rest lightly on the child’s shoulder or steady the back of their head without pulling. A small kiss sound is audible, followed by a quiet affectionate phrase. The child may look up, smile, or remain still; their response should not be forced. Indoors, warm window light catches the curve of both faces and the slight movement of clothing as the adult straightens.

One person stands or sits beside another, close enough to reach the upper back without stretching. Their face is attentive, with slightly raised brows; their eyes check the other person’s expression, and their mouth may form a brief reassuring smile. An open palm lands flat between the shoulder blades, lifts a few centimetres, and returns in two or three gentle pats. Cloth makes soft, dull taps rather than sharp slaps. The other person’s shoulders may ease downward as they breathe out. A low phrase such as “It’s okay” can accompany the motion. In a home or gathering, the gesture is brief and leaves space for the other person to turn away.

topic: tapping a shoulder to get attention
body: A person approaches from the side or slightly behind, leaving a little space. Their face is neutral and polite; their eyes look toward the person’s face, and their mouth stays closed until they turn. Two fingertips touch the outside of the shoulder through clothing, make one or two light taps, then withdraw immediately. The contact produces only a faint fabric sound. The person being tapped turns their head first, then their shoulders, often with a quick questioning look. The tapper may say “Excuse me” in an ordinary indoor voice once eye contact is made. In a busy shop or family gathering, nearby conversation continues underneath the brief exchange.

Two people lean slightly closer without pressing against each other. The speaker’s eyes glance briefly around, then settle near the listener’s ear; their brows may lift, while their mouth forms small, precise movements. One hand can rise beside the mouth as a loose screen, not a tight cup. Air and soft consonants are audible at close range, but the words are difficult for anyone farther away to hear. The listener tilts their head, keeps their body still for a few seconds, then may smile or raise their eyebrows. In a bright café or living room, the quiet exchange contrasts with dishes, footsteps, or conversation in the background.

A person spots someone on the opposite pavement and turns their whole torso toward them. Their chin lifts, eyes narrow slightly to focus at a distance, and their mouth opens wide for a short call, often a name followed by a few words. One hand rises above shoulder height and waves in broad arcs so the movement reads across traffic. Their voice projects from the chest with a louder, longer vowel than ordinary conversation; passing cars or market noise partly mask it. They pause to see whether the other person turns before calling again. Sunlight outlines the raised arm, while the street remains between them.

During an animated Iraqi conversation, the speaker faces the listener with alert eyes and brows that rise or draw together to match the point being made. Their mouth shapes words at a conversational pace, with short pauses for a nod or a reply. Open palms turn upward to present an idea; fingers gather briefly to mark a detail, then the hands spread apart to show size or distance. The wrists stay loose, and each movement starts near the chest before extending outward. Clothing rustles softly beneath the voices. The listener may nod or answer with a small hand motion. Gestures vary by person and situation, from restrained to lively.

A storyteller sits or stands facing a small group, leaning forward as the scene grows interesting. Their eyes move from one listener to another; eyebrows lift at a surprising turn, and the mouth briefly holds a smile before continuing. Hands sketch a path through the air, mark a person’s height, or open wide to show a space. They pause mid-gesture for a beat, then bring the hands down as the next sentence lands. The voice shifts in pace and pitch, with a soft chuckle or audible breath between lines. Listeners watch, smile, or lean in. Warm room light catches the moving hands against clothing.

Two familiar people trade short, quick replies while remaining close and relaxed. Their eyebrows rise in exaggerated disbelief, but their eyes stay bright and return to each other’s faces. Mouths curve into half-smiles even while each person insists on a point. One lifts an open palm as if objecting; the other points briefly at an object or counts on their fingers, then lets the hand fall. Their voices overlap for a moment, louder than normal conversation but without a harsh, sustained shout. A laugh, snort, or smiling exhale breaks the exchange. Shoulders stay loose, and both leave pauses for the other to answer.

Two friends sit close enough to hear each other over the low murmur of a café. One notices a harmless detail, such as the other’s carefully arranged hair, and lifts their eyebrows before delivering a short, playful remark. Their eyes stay on their friend’s face, checking the reaction. A crooked smile appears, followed by a brief chuckle; one hand makes a small pointing motion, then drops. The friend rolls their eyes but smiles back. The teasing stops if that smile fades. Cups touch the tabletop with light taps under warm indoor light.

A crying friend sits with shoulders drawn inward, wet lower eyelids and uneven breaths. The other person sits beside them rather than blocking their view, leaning slightly closer. Their eyebrows soften, eyes meet the friend’s briefly, and their mouth stays relaxed as they speak in a low, unhurried voice: “I’m here.” They offer a tissue in an open hand and wait; if welcomed, they rest a hand lightly on the friend’s shoulder. There is a quiet sniffle, the rustle of tissue and room noise. Neither person needs to smile. Soft window light catches the tears without exaggerating them.

The person faces the one they hurt at conversational distance, with shoulders lowered and hands still or loosely held together. Their eyebrows draw slightly inward; their eyes meet the other person’s, then dip briefly without looking away for long. The mouth opens on a quiet, clear apology, naming what they did rather than making excuses. Their voice is steady but subdued, with a small pause afterward to let the words land. They do not reach for a hug or demand an answer. A breath is audible in the pause; ordinary room sounds continue around them in plain daylight.

After an apology, the listener’s tight jaw loosens and their eyes soften. They say, “I forgive you,” in a quiet voice, then open both arms and wait for the other person to step forward. Their mouths form small, relieved smiles. The embrace closes gently: arms wrap around upper backs, shoulders touch, and both bodies settle their weight without squeezing hard. A breath leaves one person’s chest; fabric brushes fabric. After a few seconds they separate enough to see each other’s faces, hands falling naturally to their sides. Warm indoor light shows the movement clearly, without turning the moment into a performance.

A person opens a door into a lit room where friends stand near a cake, paper decorations and a few balloons. As everyone calls out together, the newcomer stops mid-step. Their eyes widen, eyebrows rise and mouth opens briefly before a surprised laugh escapes. One hand goes to their chest or partly covers their mouth; the other still holds the door or a bag. They look from face to face, then smile broadly as their shoulders relax. Overlapping voices, claps and balloon squeaks fill the room. The cake candles make small warm points of light, not enough to light the whole space.

A student checks a results page on a phone or printed sheet, holding it close enough to read. Their eyes move across the name and marks, then return to the marks once more. Eyebrows lift, the mouth opens into a grin and a quick breath or soft “Yes!” comes out. Their free hand curls into a small fist near the chest; their shoulders rise, then loosen. They turn the screen or paper toward a nearby friend, who leans in to check it. The phone stays steady after the first excited movement. Daylight falls across the page amid quiet corridor chatter.

names: سمعت خبر مو زين وبقيت هادي
body: A person listens to difficult news in a quiet room, standing or sitting still. Their smile disappears; their lips press together lightly and their eyes stay on the speaker, blinking once or twice. One hand rests flat on a table or closes gently around the other hand. They take a slow breath, lower their gaze for a moment, then look back and ask a short, practical question in a controlled, softer voice. Calm does not mean unaffected: their shoulders are a little tense and there is a pause before they answer. The room’s faint background hum remains audible.

A student waits for results beside a phone on a desk. They sit forward with feet planted, shoulders slightly raised and fingers rubbing one thumb against the other. Their eyes check the phone, shift to the clock, then return to the phone after a few seconds. Lips press together; they swallow and let out a short breath through the nose. When a notification sounds, one hand reaches quickly but stops for a beat before touching the screen. The chair gives a faint creak as they lean in. Cool daylight and ordinary room noise keep the scene grounded.

A new employee stands just inside a workplace doorway, shoulders slightly raised and feet close together. Their eyes scan the room, then return to the person greeting them; a brief smile appears while the lips remain pressed at the corners. One hand grips a bag strap or folder, and the other smooths a sleeve before a tentative handshake. They inhale, pause, and answer in a quiet voice that steadies after the first few words. A small breath or nervous chuckle may follow. Office light falls across desks and polished floors; footsteps and low conversation continue behind them.

The candidate sits upright without appearing rigid, both feet on the floor and shoulders relaxed. Their eyes meet the interviewer’s for a few seconds at a time, shifting naturally when they consider a question. A small, open smile accompanies the greeting; the mouth moves clearly through measured answers. Their hands rest on the table or make compact gestures to mark a point, then settle again. They pause briefly before difficult answers rather than rushing. Their voice is even and audible, with a light inhale between sentences. In a quiet office, chair movement, paper handling and the interviewer’s responses remain soft background sounds.

A salesperson stands beside the product, angled toward the customer rather than blocking it. Their eyebrows lift, eyes move between the customer and the feature being shown, and a broad smile briefly narrows as they concentrate on a demonstration. Open hands indicate size or function; fingers touch the item gently and release it before the next point. Their gestures quicken during an exciting detail, then slow to allow a question. The voice is bright, clear and varied in pitch, not shouted. A soft click, rustle or tap from the demonstration is audible amid ordinary shop conversation and indoor lighting.

The customer looks at the purchase or finished service for a moment before reacting. Their forehead relaxes, eyes brighten, and a smile grows from closed lips into a brief glimpse of teeth. They give one or two unhurried nods, then look back at the person serving them. Their shoulders drop slightly; one hand may touch the item while the other makes a small approving gesture. A quiet laugh or pleased exhale comes before a warm, conversational thank-you. The response is not a prolonged pose: after a few seconds, they return to checking the item or gathering their belongings under normal shop lighting.

The customer lifts a spoon or small food sample steadily toward the mouth, leaning forward just enough to avoid spilling. Their lips close around the bite; the hand lowers while they chew with the mouth closed. Their eyes glance down for a second as they register the flavour, then rise toward the server. The eyebrows lift slightly, the cheeks round into a smile, and they nod twice at a natural, uneven pace. A soft appreciative hum may come after swallowing, followed by a short comment in a relaxed voice. Cutlery makes a faint clink against the plate amid low restaurant conversation.

The chef places a finished plate on a counter with both hands, lowering it carefully so it lands without a clatter. They turn the plate a few degrees to face the viewer, then withdraw their hands rather than hovering over the food. Their back straightens, shoulders settle, and their eyes move from the plating to the guest’s face. A restrained smile lifts the mouth; the eyebrows rise briefly while they name the dish in a warm, steady voice. A small exhale follows the presentation. Kitchen light catches the plate’s rim and food textures, while ventilation and distant utensil sounds remain in the background.

The artist steps back from the artwork, shifting their weight from one foot to the other to see it from a little distance. Their eyes travel across separate details, pause on one area, then take in the whole piece. The mouth softens into a small smile; the eyebrows lift or draw together briefly in concentration. One hand holds a brush, tool or cloth at their side while the other rests loosely against the hip. They lean their head a few degrees, breathe out softly and may murmur a quiet observation. Studio light reveals the surface texture; faint tool sounds fade as their hands become still.

An elderly woman sits comfortably with her hands visible in her lap or lifted to show the designs. Fine lines and soft folds mark the skin; reddish-brown henna forms patterned shapes across the palms and fingers, with colour varying where the dye has worn. She opens her hands slowly and turns them so the light reaches both sides. Her eyes follow the pattern, then meet the person beside her. Her mouth forms a gentle smile, and she speaks in a calm, textured voice, with a small breath between phrases. Fabric rustles as she moves; natural window light shows the henna without making it appear glossy.

topic: old man with prayer beads on a bench
body: An older man sits upright but relaxed on a painted metal or wooden bench, his shoulders slightly rounded and his shoes planted flat. Fine lines gather beside his eyes; his gaze rests on the path ahead, then drops to the small beads passing between his thumb and forefinger. His mouth stays gently closed, occasionally moving with a quiet murmur. One hand holds the loop while the other rests on his knee. Each bead advances with a tiny dry click, slower when he looks up. Afternoon light catches the smooth bead surfaces and the creases of his hands; footsteps and distant conversation remain in the background.

A young mother walks beside a compact stroller, one or both hands around its foam-covered handlebar. She leans forward slightly to cross uneven pavement, then straightens as the four small wheels roll smoothly again. Her eyes alternate between the path and the child beneath the fabric canopy; her face softens, her mouth forms a brief smile, and she speaks in a low, gentle voice. A loose blanket shifts with the stroller’s motion. The wheels make a faint rattle over paving seams, while a brake pedal and storage basket remain visible below. Sunlight filters through the canopy onto the seat.

A father and his school-age son stand a comfortable distance apart on a firm riverbank, each holding a slender fishing rod angled over the water. The father glances from his line to the boy’s hands and quietly points toward a float. The boy narrows his eyes at the ripples, parts his lips in concentration, then grins when the float bobs. Their elbows bend as they adjust the lines; the rod tips flex lightly rather than jerking. Small waves tap the bank, a reel clicks, and their voices stay low. Reflected daylight flickers across their sleeves and the water.

Two siblings of similar size jostle on a rug or grassy patch, leaving room around furniture and other people. One reaches toward the other’s shoulder; the other steps back, raises open hands and dodges. Their eyebrows lift, their eyes stay on each other, and their mouths spread into unmistakable smiles between short bursts of laughter. They make brief, light contact and release it immediately, shifting their weight with small, quick steps. Fabric rustles and feet scuff the surface; one calls out in a teasing voice and the other answers. A nearby adult can be present, watching calmly.

Two close friends sit side by side at a café table or stand together on a walkway. One finishes a sentence, eyes bright and eyebrows raised; a beat later the other breaks into laughter, mouth open and cheeks lifted. Both briefly look at each other, then glance away as the laughter grows. Their shoulders bounce, one hand covers a smile while the other taps the table or a friend’s sleeve. The sound comes in uneven, breathy bursts, with a few half-spoken words between them. Cups may tremble slightly on the table. Soft daylight shows natural creases around their eyes.

Two newlyweds walk together after a celebration, close enough for their sleeves to brush. Their clothing is neat and festive: a tailored suit or formal outfit beside a dress or other carefully chosen wedding attire, without assuming one particular style. Their steps gradually fall into rhythm; joined hands swing a few centimetres between them. One turns to the other with lifted cheeks and a small smile, and the other answers softly while glancing from their partner’s face back to the path. Shoes make alternating taps on paving. Evening light glints on a ring or fabric detail, with distant guests talking behind them.

A teacher stands beside a seated student at a classroom desk, both focused on an open workbook. The teacher bends slightly to the student’s eye level, points to one line without covering the page, and speaks in a measured, clear voice. Their expression is attentive, with relaxed brows and steady eye contact when the student looks up. The student follows the line with a finger, presses their lips together while thinking, then gives a small nod and answers. A pencil makes a short scratch across paper; a chair shifts softly. Window light falls across the desk, with other desks blurred behind them.

A doctor sits facing a patient in a clean consultation room, close enough for conversation but leaving comfortable personal space. The doctor’s shoulders are relaxed, their face attentive and their eyes level with the patient’s. They speak slowly in a calm, even voice, pausing after a short explanation. An open hand indicates a simple diagram or notes rather than gesturing sharply. The patient initially holds their hands together and looks down; as they listen, their grip loosens, their eyes rise and their mouth settles into a small, relieved smile. Paper shifts quietly on the desk, with soft room ventilation underneath.

A nurse in clean scrubs stands beside a patient’s bed under soft clinic lighting. The face relaxes before the smile appears: cheeks lift slightly, the mouth corners turn up without showing many teeth, and the eyes narrow gently while staying attentive to the patient. One hand rests lightly on a bed rail; the other holds a chart or remains open at waist height. The body leans forward a little, then settles still. The nurse speaks in a low, even voice, with a quiet breath between sentences. Fabric rustles softly as they shift position.

A farmer stands at the edge of a field in a faded cotton shirt, with fine dust on the sleeves. The face has uneven tanning and small creases around the eyes and mouth; the eyes squint briefly toward the bright sky, then return to the ground ahead. Dry lips part for a short reply, and the mouth closes as the farmer listens. One hand shades the brow while the other rests on a tool handle, without gripping it tightly. The shoulders sit slightly forward. A breeze moves loose fabric and crops nearby; footsteps press softly into dry soil, and the voice sounds steady and unhurried.

A fisherman sits beside a small boat or on a dock, sorting a damp net. The hands have rough fingertips, shallow creases and pale, softened patches where wet rope has rubbed the skin. Fingers pinch a knot, pull the line taut, then release it; the net falls back with a light scrape. The face stays intent, eyes following each loop, mouth closed except for a brief, quiet answer. Shoulders lean over the work and straighten between knots. Water taps against the hull, rope rasps against the palms, and a breeze lifts the edges of a practical shirt.

topic: taxi driver with arm out the window
body: A taxi driver waits at the curb with the side window fully lowered. One forearm lies loosely along the window ledge, the hand hanging just outside with relaxed fingers; the other hand rests near the steering wheel. The driver sits upright but not rigidly, glancing toward the road, then briefly toward a passenger. The eyes track traffic, and the mouth opens for a short, matter-of-fact reply before closing again. Engine vibration makes the resting arm shift faintly. Street noise and a distant horn pass through the open window; the voice sounds conversational rather than raised.

A gamer sits close enough to see a screen clearly, its changing light reflected softly in the eyes. The brows draw together for a moment; the eyes make quick, small movements across the display. Lips press lightly together, then part on a quiet exhale. Fingers make short, precise taps on keys or controller buttons while the wrists stay mostly steady. The upper body leans forward during a tense moment and eases back when it passes. Button clicks, a chair creak and low game audio accompany a brief spoken phrase, delivered without looking away from the screen.

An athlete has just left the playing area, wearing a damp team shirt with fabric clinging at the shoulders. The chest rises and falls quickly, then more slowly over several breaths. Hands rest on the hips or briefly on the knees; the body bends forward and gradually straightens. The eyes blink against sweat and settle on someone speaking nearby. The mouth stays open for air before forming a few short words in a breathy voice. Shoes scuff the floor, and background voices remain indistinct. The expression shows physical fatigue without assuming whether the match was won or lost.

A runner approaches a painted finish line at speed, arms pumping close to the torso and feet striking in alternating, quick steps. The eyes aim past the line; the face tightens with effort, brows drawn and mouth open for fast breaths. As the leading foot lands beyond the marking, the body continues forward rather than stopping abruptly. The arms drop gradually, stride length shortens, and the runner bends slightly while catching breath. Shoes slap the track, clothing flutters with each step, and spectators sound distant behind the runner’s breathing. Any finish tape appears only if the event has set one up.

A runway model walks along a lit catwalk with a composed expression suited to the garment being shown. The gaze stays level toward the far end, shifting only slightly at the turn; the brows remain relaxed and the mouth rests closed or gently parted. The chin stays steady as the shoulders move subtly with each measured step. Hands hang naturally unless the outfit calls for holding a bag or adjusting a coat. At the end, the model pauses for a beat, turns, then resumes walking. Footsteps sound against the runway beneath low music; speech is usually absent, and the fabric moves according to its weight.

An influencer faces a phone held at arm’s length or set upright on a small tripod. Their face stays angled toward the front camera; their eyes meet the lens, then briefly check the screen. Eyebrows lift to emphasize a point, and the mouth forms clear words with occasional quick smiles. One hand steadies the phone while the free hand makes small, timed gestures before returning to rest. The shoulders remain relaxed, with slight head tilts and natural pauses between phrases. Their voice sounds close to the phone microphone, with soft breaths and faint finger taps on the case. Window light or a ring light creates small reflections in the eyes.

A news presenter sits upright behind a desk or stands with weight evenly balanced. The back is straight without looking rigid, shoulders level and lowered, and the chin nearly parallel to the floor. Their face holds a composed expression; eyes look steadily into the camera or briefly down at notes before returning. The mouth moves precisely through each sentence, with short pauses and restrained eyebrow movements. Hands rest lightly on the desk or meet near the waist, opening occasionally for a measured gesture. Clothing lies smoothly with little shifting. The voice is clear and even; breaths are quiet, while paper may make a faint rustle under soft studio lighting.
